example_sentences_in_english: His writing shows the fault of guru-chandali, confusing the readers.
Modern Bengali literature tries to avoid guru-chandali.
history: This term critiques the linguistic style of 19th-century Bengali literature, notably used to describe Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's language as afflicted with guru-chandali dosh.

It draws from caste-based purity concepts, with examples like mixed terms: charby-choshya ranna (cooking of chewable-suckable), bhatprashan (rice-eating), mrityadaha (corpse-burning), shabpoda (corpse-cremation).
note: Refers to a specific linguistic impurity in Bengali prose evolution.
